purpose: Every default-selection test launch site that starts Python or passes a prepared command, with how its child is shown not to reach the real application folders. Kept complete by test_run_context_child_sites.py.

dispositions.census: Observed in an ordinary pytest run with the census hook: the child never asked for the real known folders. The census is an acceptance check at the candidate; its receipt names each test that launched a child.
dispositions.tripwire_at_site: The test loads the child tripwire before the child's own program and asserts zero real-adapter calls.
dispositions.guard_built_by_test: The test builds the child's environment to carry the MAIN-5 guard.
dispositions.nested_pytest: The child is a pytest session of this repository and applies the same run context to itself.
dispositions.nested_pytest_passive: The child is a pytest session that executes no repository test.
dispositions.native_helper_only: The child imports only the native job helper.
dispositions.runner_only_plant: The launch is skipped in an ordinary run.
dispositions.non_python: The launched program is not Python.
dispositions.literal_program: The command is `python -c <program> [data...]`: the interpreter, options that select no code, the inline flag, a program that is a literal or a string constant of the module, then data; the program imports only os, sys and time and evaluates nothing, so it cannot reach the resolver. The map test reads the command in that order.
dispositions.reviewed_program: The launched program is assembled at run time by a named helper from reviewed pieces; a site-specific executable proof in test_run_context_reviewed_programs.py regenerates it with synthetic inputs, checks every statement against the reviewed shapes, runs its file-writing part in isolation, binds the helper's source and every reachable tail, and rejects any other construction. The proof names the site in PROVEN_SITES.
dispositions.posix_only_caller: The launch sits inside a test that skips on Windows; it is not reachable in the Windows default selection.

keyring_verdicts.non_python: The launched program is not Python and runs none of this repository's code (git, docker, a hook binary).
keyring_verdicts.literal_program: The literal-program check above limits the program to imports of os, sys and time: it cannot import keyring.
keyring_verdicts.reviewed_program: The reviewed-program proof holds every statement to shapes that import only os, sys, time and subprocess, and launch only those programs: nothing imports keyring.
keyring_verdicts.not_in_default_run: The launch is skipped in an ordinary run (runner-only plant).
keyring_verdicts.nested_pytest: The child is a pytest session over this repository's tests, so the root conftest installs keyring's fail backend in it and in each of its xdist workers (#538). Its own launches are sites of this map.
keyring_verdicts.import_closure: Every module the child's entries can import, lazy imports included, imports keyring nowhere, and nothing in that closure imports or runs code by a computed name. The map test recomputes the closure from the sources each run (tests.support.child_keyring.import_closure).
keyring_verdicts.fail_backend_in_child_env: The child's environment selects keyring's fail backend through PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND (tests.support.child_keyring.environment, which the child tripwire's environments also apply). The map test finds that call in the launching function or in the helper named by control_in. A tripwire site's child also records the selection and the parent's check requires it.

mechanisms.tool:git: git runs no Python of this repository; the fixtures' hooks are not installed in the temporary repositories these launches use.
mechanisms.tool:docker: docker runs containers, not this repository's Python on the host.
